messages.subject_clean: devtools test() complains about missing testthat folder
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

when I run

> library(test_that)
> test_dir("test")

my testthat tests are executed,

but

> library(devtools)
> test()

complains about

     Error: No testthat directories found in /home/uweschmitt/r_projects/uwetest/R/test_package

In both cases my working directory is the one given in the error message.

Any hints ?

Regards, Uwe

messages.subject: Re: devtools test() complains about missing testthat folder
messages.subject_clean: devtools test() complains about missing testthat folder
messages.body_plain:
Hi Uwe,

On 4 Apr 2014, at 14:56, Uwe Schmitt wrote:

>
> > library(test_that)
> > test_dir("test")

Your tests are not in a standard location. Your package needs to have a folder:

tests/testthat <https://github.com/jefferis/nat/tree/master/tests/testthat>

(or, no longer recommended, inst/tests)

containing your tests.

> > library(devtools)
> > test()

This will work now.

You can also have

check()

run your tests if you have a script like

tests/test-all.R

library(testthat)
test_check("<name_of_mypackage>")

There are lots of examples on github with this organisation. e.g.

https://github.com/jefferis/flycircuit

Best,

Greg.

--
Gregory Jefferis, PhD
Division of Neurobiology
MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology
Francis Crick Avenue
Cambridge Biomedical Campus
Cambridge, CB2 OQH, UK

http://www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/group-leaders/h-to-m/g-jefferis
http://www.neuroscience.cam.ac.uk/directory/profile.php?gsxej2
http://flybrain.stanford.edu

messages.subject: strange errors when running tests from devtools
messages.subject_clean: strange errors when running tests from devtools
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I observed some strange errors when using test() from devtools.

The minimal test file is
>
> test_that("open file", {
>           require(mzR)
>           con <- openMSfile("mini.mzML")
>           close(con)
> })

and running this test yields the following output

> $ R --quiet --vanilla <<EOL
> library(devtools)
> test()
> EOL
>
> > library(devtools)
>
> Attaching package: ‘devtools’
>
> The following objects are masked from ‘package:utils’:
>
>     ?, help
>
> The following object is masked from ‘package:base’:
>
>     system.file
>
> > test()
> Loading required package: testthat
> Testing reproduce_error
> Loading reproduce_error
> Invalid DESCRIPTION:
> Malformed package name
>
> See the information on DESCRIPTION files in section 'Creating R
> packages' of the 'Writing R Extensions' manual.
>
> Loading required package: mzR
> Loading required package: Rcpp
> 1
>
> 1. Error: open file ------------------------------------------------------------
> no applicable method for 'close' applied to an object of class "c('mzRramp', 'mzR', 'Versioned')"
> 1: close(con) at test00.r:4
>
> Warning message:
> class "C++Object" is defined (with package slot ‘Rcpp’) but no metadata object found to revise subclass information---not exported?  Making a copy in package ‘.GlobalEnv’
> >

If I run testthat it works:

> $ R --quiet --vanilla <<EOL
> library(testthat)
> test_dir("tests/testthat")
> EOL
>
> > library(testthat)
> > test_dir("tests/testthat")

You can find the minimal setup at https://github.com/uweschmitt/reproduce_error

Any idea what's going on ? The failure is not specifically related to the used mzR package,
I observed it before in another context.

Kind Regards,

Uwe
